items: PART B — PRINCIPLES OF INDIAN FOREIGN POLICY
Meaning: a sense of oneness/unity overriding divisive identities (region, religion, caste, language).

groups.heading: ADVANCED LIMIT
items: Constitutional basis: Article 51 (DPSP) — promote international peace, honourable inter-state relations,
NOT: The NIC is a constitutional/statutory body → extra-constitutional, non-statutory advisory body (est. 1961).
NOT: Foreign policy has no constitutional basis → Article 51 (DPSP) provides the directive foundation.
NOT: Panchsheel was signed with the USSR → with China (1954, Tibet Treaty) , Nehru–Zhou Enlai.

groups.heading: COMPARATIVE NUANCE
items: NOT: India signed the NPT/CTBT → India has not signed either (calls them discriminatory).
NOT: NAM means neutrality/isolation → it means an independent stance, not neutrality or non-involvement.
NOT: India cut ties with South Africa in 1947 → in 1954 (over apartheid).
CAUTION: NIC is effectively defunct — its last (16th) meeting was in 2013 ; it has not been reconstituted since 2014 .
